newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares finish higher, outlook unclear.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares finish higher, outlook unclear.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Monday after a quiet day's trading, following foreign stock and bond markets, with dealers seeing another dull day ahead with moderate rises or falls expected.
"There is little prospect of much activity tomorrow either. The KFX index could swing a quarter point up or down by the end of the day," one dealer said.
The top-20 KFX index gained 0.37 point to 127.13, ending a week of decline while the KFX December future rose 0.50 point to 128.10 with 30 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded
Much interest focused again on third biggest bank BG Bank, which is expected to join the ranks of the KFX top-20 index in November, with 165,000 shares changing hands to close 1.9 crowns up at 255.
Leading banks Den Danske and Unidanmark both benefited from the interest in BG Bank, ending one and two crowns up at 420 and 272 respectively. SAS also attracted interest, finishing 0.50 up at 74.
Overall turnover for the day was 614 million crowns.
